query: I am a private sector salaried employee working in Delhi. How is my House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption limit calculated under the 1962 rules?
persona_context: Private sector salaried employee residing in Delhi (metro city)
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 2A of the Income Tax Rules 1962, the HRA exemption for a salaried employee in Delhi (a metro city) is the least of: (a) actual HRA received, (b) rent paid in excess of 10% of salary, or (c) 50% of salary (since Delhi is a metro city; non-metros are 40%).
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 2A
States 50% of salary for Delhi (metro)
States rent paid minus 10% of salary
States actual HRA received
Specifies least of the three is exempt

query: I am an employee claiming Leave Travel Concession (LTC) for a vacation in Singapore. Is my international flight exempt under Rule 2B?
persona_context: Salaried employee traveling abroad on holiday
ground_truth_answer: No. Under Rule 2B of the Income Tax Rules 1962, Leave Travel Concession (LTC) exemption under section 10(5) is strictly limited to travel to any place within India. Foreign/international travel expenses are not exempt.
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 2B / Section 10(5)
States LTC is strictly restricted to travel within India
Denies exemption for overseas / Singapore travel

query: I work for a private company that provided me with a 1.8-litre engine car for both official and personal use, and the company pays all running and maintenance expenses. What is the monthly perquisite value added to my salary under Rule 3?
persona_context: Corporate manager with company-owned car (> 1.6L cubic capacity) used partly for personal purposes with employer-borne running expenses
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3(2) Table (Sl. No. 1(1)(c)(ii)), where a motor car exceeding 1.6 litres cubic capacity is owned or hired by the employer, running and maintenance expenses are met by the employer, and it is used partly for official and partly for personal purposes, the perquisite value is Rs. 2,400 per month (plus Rs. 900 per month if a chauffeur/driver is provided).
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 3(2)
Identifies cubic capacity category (> 1.6 litres / 1600cc)
States monthly perquisite value of Rs. 2,400
Notes additional Rs. 900 per month if chauffeur is provided

query: Under the 2026 rules (Rule 280), if an employee opts for the new tax regime under section 202(4), which specific allowances remain exempt?
persona_context: Salaried employee operating under the 2026 direct tax regime exercising section 202(4) option
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 280(3) of the Income Tax Rules 2026, an employee who has exercised an option under section 202(4) is entitled to exemption ONLY in respect of allowances mentioned in sub-rule (1)(a) to (d) (travel/transfer allowance, tour daily allowance, conveyance allowance, helper allowance) and in sub-rule (2) [Table: Sl. No. 10] (transport allowance for visually impaired or orthopedically disabled employees).
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 280(3)
References Section 202(4)
Specifies sub-rule (1)(a)-(d) allowances (travel, daily, conveyance, helper)
Specifies sub-rule (2) Sl. No. 10 (disability transport allowance)

query: How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 3 (1962 rules)?
persona_context: Salaried employee with company loan under 1962 rules
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3 of the 1962 rules, the value of an interest-free or concessional loan is determined on the basis of the maximum monthly balance at the rate charged by State Bank of India. However, loans for medical treatment of specified diseases or petty loans not exceeding Rs. 20,000 are completely exempt from perquisite valuation.
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 3
Refers to SBI benchmark lending rate
Mentions Rs. 20,000 threshold or medical treatment exemption

query: Compare the valuation of company accommodation perks between 1962 Rule 3 and 2026 Rule 15 for a private sector employee in a major metro with population > 40 lakhs.
persona_context: Corporate employee analyzing rent-free accommodation valuation across 1962 and 2026 regimes
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 3 of the 1962 rules (post-2023 amendment), the perquisite value of employer-owned accommodation in cities having population > 40 lakhs as per the 2011 census is 10% of salary. Under Rule 15 of the 2026 rules, the valuation follows the modernized schedule under Section 15 with aligned population tiers and salary definitions.

query: What are the procedural steps to calculate tax relief under Rule 21A for salary received in arrears under section 89?
persona_context: Government / PSU employee receiving 3 years of salary arrears in a single lump sum
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 21A(1) and (2) of the Income Tax Rules 1962: (1) Calculate tax on total income including arrears in the year of receipt, (2) Calculate tax on total income excluding arrears in the year of receipt, to find the tax difference [A], (3) For each year to which arrears relate, calculate tax including and excluding additional salary to find tax difference [B], (4) Relief equals [A] minus [B] (if positive). The employee must furnish particulars in Form No. 10E under Rule 21AA.
evaluation_criteria: Mentions Rule 21A and Section 89
Explains Step 1 & 2 (tax with and without arrears in receipt year)
Explains Step 3 & 4 (tax in respective previous years)
Cites Form No. 10E under Rule 21AA

query: Under Rule 12 (1962 rules), what is the procedural eligibility condition to file return in Form SAHAJ (ITR-1) for a salaried resident individual?
ground_truth_answer: Under Rule 12 of the 1962 rules, an individual being a resident other than not ordinarily resident having total income up to fifty lakh rupees, comprising income from salary, one house property, and income from other sources (such as interest), is eligible to file return of income in Form No. SAHAJ (ITR-1).
